newsitem.title: FRANCE: 30 French police hurt in clashes over immigration.
newsitem.headline: 30 French police hurt in clashes over immigration.

text.p: Thirty riot police were hurt -- including one who lost a finger -- and 40 protesters detained during overnight clashes in Paris over new French immigration legislation, police said on Wednesday.

Two officers were taken to hospital, one with a severed finger, the other with facial injuries, while the other 38 suffered only slight injuries in the street battles. Police said they had no figures for injuries to demonstrators.
Five of the 40 people detained were still in custody on Wednesday, three suspected of violence against police and two for damaging public property.

The clashes erupted near the National Assembly between a few hundred demonstrators hurling stones and other projectiles, after a march through the capital against a controversial bill under debate in parliament to tighten French immigration laws.
Police said the march drew 16,000 people, the organisers said 30,000.

Police in the southern city of Toulouse used tear gas to disperse demonstrators overnight who were protesting against the law and against a public meeting by the number two of the far-right National Front, Bruno Megret, in the city.
Toulouse police said five police officers were injured.

The controversial bill, opposed by the leftist opposition and groups from artists to human rights campaigners, aims to close loopholes in existing tough laws dating from 1993 and would grant the police extended powers to track immigrants in France.
